items.title: How to avoid environment creation race conditions?
items.reason: Related creation race: parallel inline-script runs observe an incomplete environment, and a maintainer recommends locking creation and mutation. It concerns a shared script directory failing validation, whereas this report concerns successful uvx builds leaving redundant archives.

items.title: Add relocatable installs to support concurrency-safe cached environments
items.reason: Introduced building cached environments separately in archive-v0 and publishing them through a content-addressed symlink. Merged in July 2024 to fix in-use environment mutation tracked by astral-sh/uv#5503; it did not promise to deduplicate concurrent builds, so this report does not establish a regression of that fix.

items.title: Add automatic pruning of unreferenced cache archives
items.reason: Directly addresses secondary accumulation: proposes preview-gated automatic cleanup of unreferenced archives and cached tool environments unused for a week, with protection for running commands. It remains unmerged and does not serialize same-key environment creation.

items.title: uv cache management strategies for always-growing caches?
items.reason: Tracks cache growth as dependency versions change and requests retention or eviction policies. A comment reports roughly 270 GB from AWS MCP servers, closely matching the secondary impact, but does not establish concurrent duplicate environment creation.

items.title: uv cache size limit
items.reason: Canonical size-limit and garbage-collection discussion, with MCP-related disk-growth reports and references to the open automatic-pruning proposal. Broader than preventing redundant builds or evicting superseded tool environments.

items.title: Support proactive cache pruning
items.reason: Requests configurable periodic pruning during normal commands because users forget manual cleanup. Matches the report's cleanup-discoverability concern, but neither identifies nor fixes the concurrent uvx build race.

items.title: Ephemeral environments are not ephemeral
items.reason: Reports persistent cached script environments and disk growth. Maintainers explain that ephemeral does not mean deleted after execution and point to astral-sh/uv#5731. Its environments are keyed by different script paths, unlike redundant uvx environments for one resolution.

related.search_scope: Separated concurrent cold-cache duplication from superseded-version retention and automatic cleanup. Searched open/closed issues and open/closed/merged PRs using uvx/tool run, concurrent/parallel, cold cache, orphan/duplicate environments, environments-v2, archive-v0, CachedEnvironment, superseded/old versions, cache growth, locking, and auto/proactive pruning; also checked closed uvx/0.13.7/cache reports. PR keyword searches returned no entries, so supplemented them with all open PRs, the 400 most recently updated closed PRs including merges, and directly inspected historical references, comments, and reviews. Followed astral-sh/uv#5503 to astral-sh/uv#5509 and astral-sh/uv#5731 through closed astral-sh/uv#17211 to open astral-sh/uv#20116. Ruled out astral-sh/uv#7184 as an unreproduced duplicate-binary report, astral-sh/uv#21374 because its manual wheel-aging proposal explicitly retains cached environments, and the historical in-use-mutation fix as evidence of a deduplication regression.

type_reason: The checkout source permits concurrent misses for the same resolved environment key to build independently, persist under fresh archive IDs, and replace the same cache link without reclaiming the displaced archive. This establishes the reported redundant-build/orphan behavior without requiring a new reproduction. No inspected issue or PR tracks that specific uvx failure closely enough to centralize it. The script race in astral-sh/uv#17399 is distinct, and astral-sh/uv#5509 fixed in-use mutation rather than duplicate creation. The secondary retention request overlaps existing enhancements but does not change the primary bug classification.
summary: No exact duplicate found. astral-sh/uv#17399 covers a different script-creation race; merged astral-sh/uv#5509 explains the archive/link design. Open astral-sh/uv#20116 and the cache-management issues cover the separate retention and automatic-cleanup request.
draft_response:
The source supports the race you describe: concurrent cache misses can each build an environment, save it under a fresh archive ID, and replace the same cache link. There is no per-key creation lock in that path. This is a bug distinct from the inline-script failure in astral-sh/uv#17399.

The next step is to test concurrent creation for one resolved environment key and coordinate those builds so they reuse one environment. For now, run `uv cache prune` after stopping long-running `uvx` processes; pruning otherwise waits for them.

Cleanup of superseded resolutions is a separate retention concern tracked in astral-sh/uv#9790 and astral-sh/uv#5731. astral-sh/uv#20116 proposes automatic pruning, including unused cached tool environments, but remains unmerged.
